name: Dihexa
title: HGF-related neural research
mechanism: Dihexa potentiates HGF/MET signaling — a pathway that drives synapse formation — and in rodent models strengthened memory circuits. Its potency in forming synapses is exactly why unsupervised human use is a leap: there are no human trials at all.
scope: Highlighted brain anatomy provides context for experimental work.

verdict: Builds synapses in rodents; no human data at all. Handle with respect.

name: Acetyl Hexapeptide-8
title: Expression-line research
mechanism: Applied to skin, it competes with the SNARE proteins that dock neurotransmitter vesicles, slightly reducing the muscle micro-contractions behind expression lines. Human cosmetic studies show real but modest wrinkle-depth reductions — nothing like injected botulinum.
scope: Skin is shown as anatomical context. The model does not include facial expression muscles or the SNARE machinery this peptide is studied against; those act at a scale below whole-body anatomy.

name: RU58841
title: Androgen-receptor research
mechanism: RU58841 blocks androgen receptors in scalp hair follicles, shielding them from DHT — the hormone that miniaturizes follicles in pattern loss — with the goal of acting locally without systemic hormone effects. Its clinical development stopped, so quality-controlled human data never arrived.
scope: Skin appendages provide anatomical context; individual scalp follicles are not segmented.

name: Testosterone / TRT
title: Androgen signaling & feedback
mechanism: Testosterone activates androgen receptors in muscle, bone, brain, and marrow, restoring lean mass, bone density, libido, and mood in genuinely deficient men — the strongest human evidence base on this page. The same receptor breadth is why oversight and monitoring matter.
scope: Research populations, formulations, clinical outcomes, and monitoring are specified in the sources.
